        Content from Why Learn Scheme

        Last updated on 2026-10-30 | Edit this page

        Overview

        Questions

        • Why learn Scheme?

        Objectives

        • Understand how Scheme relates to other programming languages
        • Know about some Scheme implementations
        • Query different types in Scheme

        Introduction

        Scheme is a programming language within the lisp family of programming languages. There are many implementations of Scheme, this lesson will use Gambit Scheme.

        Challenge

        Challenge 1: Can you do it?

        What is the output of this command?

        SCHEME 

        (display "Hello World!\n")

        OUTPUT 

        Hello World!

        Types in Scheme

        SCHEME 

        (string? "abc")

        SCHEME 

        (string? 123)

        SCHEME 

        (string? "123")

        SCHEME 

        (integer? 123)

        SCHEME 

        (integer? "123")

        SCHEME 

        (boolean? #t)

        SCHEME 

        (flonum? 0.123)

        SCHEME 

        (fixnum? 12)

        SCHEME 

        (number? 12.1)

        SCHEME 

        (rational? 5/6)

        SCHEME 

        (real? 2+3i)

        SCHEME 

        (complex? 2+3i)

        SCHEME 

        (char? #\g)
        Challenge

        Challenge 2: Can you do it?

        What is the output of this command?

        SCHEME 

        (string? (number->string (+ 3 6)))

        OUTPUT 

        #t
        Key Points
        • Scheme is a part of the Lisp family of programming languages
        • There are several implementations of Scheme, choose one appropriate for your needs

        Content from Variables and Procedures

        Last updated on 2026-10-30 | Edit this page

        Overview

        Questions

        • How do you use variables and procedures in Scheme?

        Objectives

        • Explore differences between Gambit Scheme and Guile Scheme

        Introduction

        An alternative implementation of the exercies in variables and procedres section of the Spritely Scheme Primer ported to Gambit Scheme.

        SCHEME 

        (define (chatty-add chatty-name . nums)                                                   
     (string-append chatty-name ", If you add these together you get " (number->string (apply + nums)) "!\n"))

        SCHEME 

        (define (shopkeeper thing-to-buy    
           #!optional (how-many 1)
           (cost 20)
           #!key (shopkeeper "Sammy")
           (store "Plentiful Great Produce"))
           (display
            (string-append "You walk into "
                           store
                           ", grab something from the shelves,\n"
                           "and walk up to the counter.\n\n"
                           shopkeeper
                           " looks at you and says "
                           "'"
                           (number->string how-many)
                           " "
                           thing-to-buy
                           ", eh? That will be "
                           (number->string (* cost how-many))
                           " coins!'\n")))

        SCHEME 

        (shopkeeper "apples")

        OUTPUT 

        You walk into Plentiful Great Produce, grab something from the shelves,
and walk up to the counter.

Sammy looks at you and says '1 apples, eh? That will be 20 coins!'

        SCHEME 

        (shopkeeper "bananas" 10 28)

        OUTPUT 

        You walk into Plentiful Great Produce, grab something from the shelves,
and walk up to the counter.

Sammy looks at you and says '10 bananas, eh? That will be 280 coins!'

        SCHEME 

        (shopkeeper "screws" 3 2
               shopkeeper: "Horace"
               store: "Horace's Hardware")

        OUTPUT 

        You walk into Horace's Hardware, grab something from the shelves,
and walk up to the counter.

Horace looks at you and says '3 screws, eh? That will be 6 coins!'

        Need newer version of interpreter for let-values # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77866133/how-to-use-let-values-in-gambit-scheme

        Key Points
        • Scheme implementations may differ in exact functionality offered

        Overview

        Questions

        • How do you control how your program executes?

        Objectives

        • Explain how to check whether something is true or false

        Introduction

        SCHEME 

        (define (goldilocks n smallest-ok biggest-ok)
  (cond
    ((< n smallest-ok)
     "Too small")
    ((> n biggest-ok)
     "Too big")
    (else
      "Just right!")))

        ``scheme (define a-list (list 1 2 3)) (define b-list (list 1 2 3)) (equal? a-list a-list)

        
```scheme
(eq? a-list a-list)

        SCHEME 

        (eq? a-list b-list)

        SCHEME 

        (equal? a-list b-list)

        SCHEME 

        (member 'b '(a b c))

        SCHEME 

        (member 'z '(a b c))

        SCHEME 

        (define (fruit-sleuth fruit-basket)
  (cond
   ((member fruit-basket)
    "Found the fruit you are looking for!")
   (else
     "Fruit not found. Gadzooks!"))

        SCHEME 

        (define (fruit-basket '(apple banana lemon))
(fruit-sleuth 'banana fruit-basket)

        SCHEME 

        (fruit-sleuth 'orange fruit-basket)
        Key Points
        • Program flow can be controlled by evaluating statements and checking conditions

 (string-append "Hello " name "!"))

  (string-append "Hello " name "!"))

        SCHEME 

        (quote foo)

        '(lambda (x) (* x 2))

        SCHEME 

        (quote (lambda (x) (* x 2)))

        SCHEME 

        (define animal-noises
  '((cat . meow)
    (dog . woof)
    (sheep . baa)))

        SCHEME 

        (assoc 'cat animal-noises)

        SCHEME 

        (assoc 'cow animal-noises)

        SCHEME 

        (define (cat-years years)
 (cond
  ((<= years 1)
   (* years 15))
  ((<= years 2)
   (+ 15 (* 9 (- years 1))))
  (else
   (+ 24 (* 4 (- years 2))))))

        SCHEME 

        (define (cat-entry name age)
  `(cat (name ,name)
        (age ,age)
        (cat-years-age ,(cat-years age))))

        SCHEME 

        (cat-entry "Rose" 16)

        SCHEME 

        (cat-entry "Hightower" 22)
        Challenge

        Challenge 1: Can you do it?

        What is the output of this command?

        SCHEME

        Hello World!
        Key Points
        • Lists are a fundamental part of scheme programming
        • Quotes can be used to create a list
        • Quasiquotes and commas can be used to convert from data to code

        Content from Closures

        Last updated on 2026-10-30 | Edit this page

        Overview

        Questions

        • How can we define procedures with some pre-specified input arguments?

        Objectives

        • Avoid repetitive procedure argument entry

        SCHEME 

        (define (make-goldilocks smallest-ok biggest-ok)
 (define (goldilocks n)
  (cond
   ((< n smallest-ok)
    "Too small!")
   ((> n biggest-ok)
    "Too big!")
    (else
     "Just right!")))
    goldilocks)

        SCHEME 

        (make-goldilocks 10 30)

        SCHEME 

        (define goldi
 (make-goldilocks 10 30))

        SCHEME 

        (goldi 7)

        SCHEME 

        (goldi 256)

        SCHEME 

        (goldi 22)

        SCHEME 

        (define (abstract-cons car-data cdr-data)
 (lambda (method)
  (cond
   ((eq? method 'car)
    car-data)
   ((eq? method 'cdr)
    (cdr-data)
   (else (error "Unknown method:" method)))))

        SCHEME 

        (define our-cons (abstract-cons 'foo 'bar))

        SCHEME 

        (our-cons 'car)

        SCHEME 

        (our-cons 'cdr)
        Challenge

        Challenge 1: Can you do it?

        What is the output of this command?

        SCHEME 

        (display "Hello World!\n")

        OUTPUT 

        Hello World!
        Key Points
        • Scheme allows for easy extension and modification of function behavior

        Content from Iteration and Recursion

        Last updated on 2026-10-30 | Edit this page

        Overview

        Questions

        • How can we repeatedly execute tasks in scheme?

        Objectives

        • Learn how to perform a task again with changed input arguments

        Introduction

        SCHEME 

        (string-length "cat")

        SCHEME 

        (string-length "mouse")

        SCHEME 

        (map string-length '("cat" "mouse" "cheese"))

        SCHEME 

        (define (symbol-length sym)
  (string-length (symbol->string sym)))

        SCHEME 

        (map symbol-length '(cat mouse cheese))

        SCHEME 

        (import (srfi 13)) ; string-upcase
(map (lambda (str)
      (string-append "I just love "
       (string-upcase str)
       "!!!"))
      '("oranges" "strawberries" "pineapples"))

        SCHEME 

        (for-each (lambda (str)
           (display
            (string-append "I just love "
              (string-upcase str)
              "!!!")))
             '("Pilau" "Jollof rice" "Biryani" "Paella" "Jambalaya"))

        SCHEME 

        (define (for-each proc lst)
 (cond
   ((eq? lst '())
     'done)
    (else
     ((let ((item (car lst)))
       (proc item)
       (for-each proc (cdr lst)))))))

        Add example of using above

        SCHEME 

        (define (build-tree depth)
   (cond
    ((= depth 0)
     '(0))
    (else
     (list depth
           (build-tree (- depth 1))
           (build-tree (- depth 1))))))

        SCHEME 

        (letrec ((alice
          (lambda (first?)
           (report-status "Alice" first?)
           (cond
	    (first?
	     (bob #f)))))
           (bob
            (lambda (first?)
            (report-status "Bob" first?)
            (cond
	     (first?
	      (alice #f)))))
           (report-status
            (lambda (name first?)
             (display
              (string-append name " is "
                             (cond
			      (first?
                               "first")
			       (else
                                "second"))
                              "!\n")))))
        (alice #t)
        (display "-----\n")
        (bob #t))

        SCHEME 

        (let loop ((words '("carrot" "potato" "pea" "celery"))
           (num-words 0)
	   (num-chars 0))
  (cond
   ((eq? words '())
    (display
     (string-append "We found " (number->string num-words)
                    " words and " (number->string num-chars)
		    " chars!\n")))
    (else
     (loop (cdr words)
           (+ num-words 1)
           (+ num-chars (string-length (car words)))))))
        Challenge

        Challenge 1: Can you do it?

        What is the output of this command?

        SCHEME 

        (display "Hello World!\n")

        OUTPUT 

        Hello World!
        Key Points
        • Scheme is a part of the Lisp family of programming languages
        • There are several implementations of Scheme, choose one appropriate for your needs

        Last updated on 2026-10-30 | Edit this page

        Overview

        Questions

        • How can we reassign variables?

        Objectives

        • Learn how to use set!

        SCHEME 

        (define chest 'sword)
chest

        SCHEME 

        (set! chest 'gold)
chest

        SCHEME 

        (define (make-countdown n)
 (lambda ()
  (define last-n n)
  (cond
   ((zero? n)
    0)
   (else
    (begin
     (set! n (- n 1))
      last-n)))))

        SCHEME 

        (define cdown (make-countdown 3))

        SCHEME 

        (cdown)

        SCHEME 

        (cdown)

        SCHEME

        Content from Methods

        Last updated on 2026-10-30 | Edit this page

        Overview

        Questions

        • How can we define custom extensible datatypes?

        Objectives

        • Learn how to extend scheme datatypes

        SCHEME 

        (define-structure enemy name hp)

        SCHEME 

        (define (dead? e)
(<= (enemy-hp e) 0))

        SCHEME 

        (define (damage-me e weapon hp-lost)
(cond
((dead? e)
(display (string-append "Poor " (enemy-name e) " is already dead!\n")))
(else
(enemy-hp-set! e (- (enemy-hp e) hp-lost))
(display (string-append "You attack " (enemy-name e) ", doing " (number->string hp-lost) " damage!\n")))))

        SCHEME 

        (define hobgob
(make-enemy "Hobgoblin" 25))

        SCHEME 

        (enemy-name hobgob)

        SCHEME 

        (dead? hobgob)

        SCHEME 

        (damage-me hobgob "club" 10)

        SCHEME 

        (damage-me hobgob "sword" 20)

        SCHEME 

        (damage-me hobgob "coconut" 5)

        SCHEME 

        (dead? hobgob)
        Challenge

        Challenge 1: Can you do it?

        What is the output of this command?

        SCHEME 

        (display "Hello World!\n")

        OUTPUT 

        Hello World!
        Key Points
        • Scheme allows for easy extension of datatypes
